licensing: Who Needs A Licence: All persons, except those exempt, who engage in angling, dip netting, cast netting, seining, minnow trapping, spear fishing, and bow fishing must have a Manitoba Angling Licence on their person (printed or on an electronic device; must be shown to an officer on request). Licences are not transferable or refundable.

Fees 2026: GST added at time of purchase. Manitoba Resident (age 16-64): one-day $13.00, annual $28.00. Senior (age 65+): no licence required. Active military member or veteran (Manitoba resident): no licence required. Canadian Resident (age 16+): one-day $18.00, annual $43.00. Non-Canadian Resident (age 16+): one-day $26.00, annual $69.00.

Exemptions: Manitoba resident seniors 65+ (must show proof of age and Manitoba residency). Manitoba resident active military members and veterans (must show proof of Manitoba residency plus a Canadian Forces ID, Record of Service Card, or Veterans' Service Card). Manitoba resident youth under 16 with six months' permanent residence (own licence privileges and own limit). Status Indians do not require an angling licence. Canadian/non-Canadian resident youth under 16 must fish with a licence holder (or exempt person) and their catch counts toward that person's limit; they may buy their own licence to have their own limit.

Family Fishing Weekends: June 12-14, 2026 (summer) and February 20-22, 2027 (winter). During these weekends people may fish without an angling licence anywhere in Manitoba except federal (national) parks; all other rules still apply.

Border Waters: On waters crossing the Manitoba border, anglers may have only a Manitoba limit. On specified border lakes with Ontario (Davidson, Frances, Garner, High, Mantario, Moar, Ryerson lakes) either a Manitoba or Ontario licence suffices. On Lake of the Prairies upstream of Shellmouth Dam, either a Manitoba or Saskatchewan licence suffices.
National Parks: A Manitoba Angling Licence is not valid in national parks; a federal licence is required (Parks Canada).
general_rules: Barbless hooks are mandatory in Manitoba (hooks on all lines, in use or not, must be barbless).
Anglers may use only one rod and line, except during ice fishing when two may be used; only two hooks or lures per line.
Total fish length is measured from the most anterior part of the head to the most posterior part of the tail laid flat (not pinched); 2.54 cm = 1 inch.
Harvest, possession and use of live bait fish and leeches will be prohibited as of April 1, 2027.

Live bait fish currently may not be imported into Manitoba, and may not be used or possessed in the Northwest, North Central and Northeast Divisions (including the Bloodvein and Gammon rivers); in the Southern Division live bait is allowed in some areas with exceptions (stocked trout waters, Duck Mountain, Turtle Mountain, Porcupine Provincial Forest, Whiteshell, Winnipeg River from Seven Sisters Dam to the Ontario border, Atikaki/South Atikaki parks).

Ice fishing shelters must be removed by March 14, 2027 on the Red River, March 15 in Area B of the Southern Division, March 31 in the rest of the Southern Division, and April 15 in the Northwest/North Central/Northeast Divisions.
Catching and keeping fish during a species' closed season is prohibited (must not fish for the species during its closed season).

lakes.name: Big Sand Lake
lakes.description: A remote fly-in lake in the Seal River system of far northern Manitoba, 550 miles north of Winnipeg. Big Sand Lake Lodge - the only lodge on the lake's roughly 60,000 acres of water - offers the Canadian Grand Slam: northern pike, lake trout, walleye and arctic grayling, all strict catch-and-release.

lakes.description: A Whiteshell Provincial Park lake near the Ontario border in eastern Manitoba. Anglers most commonly report northern pike, walleye and yellow perch. It sits in the same Canadian Shield lake country as Falcon and West Hawk lakes.

lakes.name: Cedar Lake
lakes.description: A large, shallow lake on the Saskatchewan River system in north-central Manitoba. It is an important commercial fishery for walleye and lake whitefish. The town of Grand Rapids sits at its north end, where the Saskatchewan River continues toward Lake Winnipeg.

towns.description: Town at the lake's north end, where Cedar Lake drains into Lake Winnipeg — full services for anglers and boaters.

towns.description: Small northern community on the lake's south shore, with a grocery store, coffee shop and department store; economy is fishing-based.

lakes.name: Clear Lake (Riding Mountain)
lakes.description: The showpiece lake of Riding Mountain National Park, Clear Lake is a moderately large, deep, spring-fed lake with exceptionally clear water. Parks Canada lists northern pike, yellow perch, walleye and lake whitefish as its prominent recreational species. The townsite of Wasagaming on its south shore is the park's commercial hub.

towns.description: Park townsite on the lake's shore inside Riding Mountain — marina with boat rentals, bait, launches, restaurants and lodging.

lakes.name: Clearwater Lake
lakes.description: A deep, clear, cold spring-fed lake in Clearwater Lake Provincial Park near The Pas, renowned for its excellent water quality and large lake trout. The nearly circular lake is 16 km across with a maximum depth of 39 m. Cold year-round temperatures slow trout growth but are essential for their survival.

towns.name: The Pas
towns.description: City on the lake's shore — full services, bait, launches, and the provincial park campground close by.

lakes.name: Cross Lake
lakes.description: A 755 km2 lake on the Nelson River in north-central Manitoba, scientifically studied for the effects of hydroelectric regulation on its fishery. Research documented lake whitefish, walleye, northern pike and cisco populations. It sits downstream of Lake Winnipeg on the Nelson River system.

towns.description: Large community where the Nelson River enters the lake, with all-weather road access and stores for groceries and supplies.

lakes.name: Crowduck Lake
lakes.description: A Whiteshell Provincial Park lake assessed by Manitoba Fisheries in 2023, holding walleye, smallmouth bass, northern pike, yellow perch, cisco and white suckers. Surveyed walleye averaged 46.8 cm, with fish up to 21 years old. It falls under the eastern region's special walleye regulation protecting fish over 45 cm.

lakes.description: A shallow prairie lake east of the town of Dauphin, between Riding Mountain and Duck Mountain, with an average depth of only 2.35 m. Annual index netting shows walleye as the dominant species, with northern pike, yellow perch, suckers and bullheads. It drains via the Mossy River into Lake Winnipegosis.

lakes.name: Falcon Lake
lakes.description: A popular Whiteshell Provincial Park lake about 152 km east of Winnipeg on the Trans-Canada Highway. Manitoba's 2022 fisheries assessment found walleye dominant at 79% of the survey catch, with northern pike, smallmouth and largemouth bass, yellow perch and lake whitefish also present. The lake is also famous for the 1967 Falcon Lake Incident UFO sighting.

towns.name: Falcon Lake
towns.description: Resort townsite right on the lake, with beaches, restaurants, a marina and boat launches.

lakes.name: Gunisao Lake
lakes.description: A trophy walleye factory in northeastern Manitoba fished by Budd's Gunisao Lake Lodge. In 2022, 65% of all Manitoba Master Angler walleyes (May-August) were caught at Gunisao, with 708 Master Angler walleyes recorded. Trophy northern pike, whitefish, suckers and perch are also caught.

This 8.0 km2 lake (max depth 30 m) holds self-sustaining lake trout plus lake whitefish, northern pike, burbot, white suckers and yellow perch. Trophy-class lake trout and whitefish have been documented.

lakes.description: A northern Manitoba fly-in lake reached by floatplane from Flin Flon, home to the five-star Kississing Lake Lodge and the drive-to Kenanow Lodge. lakes.name: Lake Athapapuskow
lakes.description: A Canadian Shield lake near Flin Flon made of three connected basins - Big Athapap, Little Athapap and the North Arm - with depths ranging from shallow flats to basins over 200 feet. It is a trophy multi-species fishery famous for lake trout, with three historical world records including a 62 lb laker. Walleye, northern pike, rainbow trout, splake and smallmouth bass round out the fishery.

lakes.description: Canada's 14th largest lake, Lake Manitoba is a very shallow prairie lake about 75 km northwest of Winnipeg. It has supported a commercial fishery since 1895 and a long-standing recreational fishery for walleye, northern pike and yellow perch. Delta Marsh at its south end is one of North America's premier waterfowl staging areas.

It supports Manitoba's most famous walleye fishery - the iridescent greenback walleye - plus a major commercial fishery where walleye is the most important species. More than 50 fish species live in the lake.

lakes.description: Manitoba's second-largest lake, Lake Winnipegosis is a shallow, turbid prairie lake west of Lake Winnipeg and north of Lake Manitoba. Anglers target walleye, smallmouth bass, northern pike and muskie, with lake trout in deep areas like Clearwater Bay.

Partly protected by Nueltin Lake Provincial Park, it is accessible only by air and fished by fly-in lodges for trophy lake trout, northern pike and arctic grayling. Lake whitefish are also common.

lakes.name: Paint Lake
lakes.description: A large, clear Canadian Shield lake just south of Thompson in Paint Lake Provincial Park, renowned for dense populations of thick-bodied walleyes. Northern pike are also abundant. Paint Lake Lodge on its shore offers cabins, a full-service restaurant and boat rentals.

lakes.name: Reed Lake
lakes.description: The largest lake in Grass River Provincial Park, Reed Lake is known for intricate shoreline, islands and fish that grow to enormous size regardless of species. Anglers target walleye, lake trout, northern pike, burbot, perch, whitefish and tullibee. Special regulations limit walleye and pike harvest in the lake and its tributaries.

lakes.name: Schist Lake
lakes.description: A lake at Flin Flon in northwest Manitoba, bordered by Bakers Narrows Provincial Park. Area anglers pursue northern pike, walleye, lake trout and perch in open water and through the ice. It is part of the Flin Flon area's network of Shield lakes.

towns.name: Flin Flon
towns.description: City right beside the lake — full services, boat launches and bait within minutes of the water.

lakes.name: Setting Lake
lakes.description: A northern Manitoba lake near Thompson listed among the province's notable drive-to walleye waters. It lies in the nickel-belt lake country of the Thompson area. Walleye are the main draw for visiting anglers.

towns.name: Thompson
towns.description: City just west of the lake on Hwy 6 — full services, and the last stop for fuel and supplies before heading to the lake.
towns.distance: west of the lake on Hwy 6

lakes.name: Wekusko Lake
lakes.description: A star-shaped lake in north-central Manitoba at the outlet of scenic Wekusko Falls, fished from Wekusko Falls Lodge. It produces thick-bodied chunky walleyes plus lake trout, northern pike, burbot, perch, whitefish and tullibee. Anglers can fish both Wekusko and nearby Reed Lake from the lodge.

towns.name: Snow Lake
towns.description: Mining town on Hwy 392 just south of the lake, with groceries, fuel, lodging and bait; Wekusko Falls Lodge (with a summer general store) sits by the falls between town and lake.

lakes.name: West Hawk Lake
lakes.description: Formed by an ancient meteorite impact, West Hawk Lake is Manitoba's deepest lake with exceptionally clear water popular for scuba diving. The crater lake in Whiteshell Provincial Park holds walleye, northern pike, yellow perch and smallmouth bass; all trout must be released and trout fishing is closed Nov 1 to Apr 15. towns.description: Resort townsite on the lake's shore with restaurants and shops in log buildings, plus beach and campground access.

lakes.name: Aikens Lake
lakes.description: Aikens Lake in Atikaki Provincial Park is a fly-in-only trophy water run by Aikens Lake Wilderness Lodge, operating since 1948 inside the UNESCO Pimachiowin Aki World Heritage site. The lodge bills it as a walleye factory with world-class trophy walleye, northern pike and lake trout, all fully guided from a floatplane base at Lac du Bonnet. The 2026 season runs late May to mid-September.

towns.name: Lac du Bonnet

lakes.name: Beautiful Lake
lakes.description: A stocked rainbow and brown trout water that doubles as the Ducks' walleye nursery. Each spring, walleye fry are stocked here and moved out as advanced fingerlings each fall for other lakes in the transfer program. The lake occasionally winterkills, which has produced exceptional growth on freshly stocked rainbows. Work the main island and the bulrushes on the south shore.

towns.name: Swan River

lakes.name: Berens Lake
lakes.description: Berens Lake is a wilderness lake on the upper Berens River in the north-basin watershed of Lake Winnipeg, a classic canoe-route lake on the historic Berens River fur-trade corridor. Paddlers report walleye and pike in the system. It is reachable by air or multi-day canoe trip, far beyond road access.

towns.name: Berens River
towns.description: Berens River First Nation is a community at the mouth of the Berens River on Lake Winnipeg's east shore. It is the nearest settlement to Berens Lake, far upstream in the wilderness.

lakes.name: Beresford Lake
lakes.description: Beresford Lake is a Nopiming campground lake once home to the 1937 Gunnar gold mine, and the 2022 fisheries assessment found walleye, northern pike, yellow perch, burbot and white sucker with walleye fry stocked in 2011. The provincial campground has 28 sites with a boat launch, and cottage development rings parts of the shore. The lake record walleye stands at 78.7 cm from 1992.

towns.name: Bissett
towns.description: Small community in eastern Manitoba; Wallace Lake Lodge sits about 19 km east of town at the last drive-to entry into the Atikaki wilderness.

lakes.name: Betula Lake
lakes.description: Betula Lake is a Whiteshell River lake known for year-round walleye fishing, and Betula Lake Resort on its shore rents boats and sells bait and tackle. The province's 2022 fisheries assessment recorded walleye, northern pike, sauger, smallmouth bass, black crappie, rock bass and yellow perch, with walleye fry stocked in most years since 2010. Nearby Pine Point Rapids and the Bannock Point petroforms make it a popular all-around destination.

towns.name: Rennie
towns.description: Small community in Whiteshell Provincial Park; the Whiteshell Natural History Museum operates nearby and the Alfred Hole Goose Sanctuary sits just east on Highway 44.

towns.name: Seven Sisters Falls
towns.description: Small community at the western edge of Whiteshell Provincial Park on the Winnipeg River; Betula Lake Resort's address is on Highway 307 here.

lakes.name: Big Bobs Lake
lakes.description: A shallow backcountry lake on the north edge of Duck Mountain Provincial Park managed for walleye and perch. Access is strictly by ATV or snowmobile along an unmaintained designated route, and launch areas are restricted to small watercraft. Check with the nearest government office for road conditions before heading in.

towns.name: Swan River
towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle before the park.

lakes.name: Bird Lake
lakes.description: Bird Lake is the southern gateway lake of Nopiming Provincial Park, with a provincial campground, boat launch, fish-cleaning facility and Nopiming Lodge within walking distance. The 2022 fisheries assessment found walleye, northern pike, smallmouth bass, yellow perch, rock bass, burbot, cisco and lake whitefish, with half a million walleye fry stocked in 2021. The Area A rule applies: all walleye over 45 cm must be released.

towns.name: Lac du Bonnet
towns.description: Town on the Winnipeg River north of the Whiteshell; Manitoba Fisheries' eastern region office is based here.

lakes.name: Black Lake
lakes.description: Black Lake in Nopiming Provincial Park has been stocked with hundreds of thousands of walleye fry in most years since 2000, and the 2022 assessment turned up walleye, northern pike, smallmouth bass, yellow perch, burbot and cisco. The lake record walleye measured 83.8 cm in 2001, and the record smallmouth hit 52.1 cm in 2022. A campground and the 5.1-mile Black Lake hiking trail make it a full-service wilderness stop.

lakes.name: Boissevain Reservoir
lakes.description: A reservoir near the town of Boissevain in the Turtle Mountain foothills, holding walleye and yellow perch according to angler catch reports. It has a main dock and boat access, and contour mapping exists for anglers who want to study its structure. A handy local option when passing through Boissevain.

towns.description: Gateway town to the Turtle Mountains with groceries, fuel, restaurants and an outdoor shop.

lakes.name: Bolton Lake
lakes.description: Bolton Lake is a northern trophy lake served by Bolton Lake Lodge & Outposts. The lodge and Hunt Fish Manitoba describe northern pike, walleye, lake trout, whitefish, and brook trout in the system. It is known for trophy fly-fishing opportunities in remote water.

lakes.name: Booster Lake
lakes.description: Booster Lake in Nopiming Provincial Park earned a provincial size-and-abundance profile for walleye, smallmouth bass and yellow perch based on 2011 and 2022 assessments. Anglers rate it for smallmouth, walleye and trophy northern pike without the crowds of the Whiteshell. It is a drive-to lake in the park's southern half.

lakes.name: Bower Lake
lakes.description: A stocked trout lake in the Turtle Mountains south of Boissevain, Bower Lake is planted with rainbow trout and also holds brown trout. As a designated stocked trout water it is open to fishing year-round. It is a popular family outing lake where a simple bait or spinner setup can produce trout close to shore.

towns.description: Gateway town to the Turtle Mountains with groceries, fuel and an outdoor shop; the service base for Bower Lake.

lakes.name: Brereton Lake
lakes.description: Brereton Lake covers 531 hectares with three boat launches, making it one of the Whiteshell's most accessible fishing lakes for northern pike, walleye, smallmouth bass and perch. Angler reports also mention lake trout, and a Master Angler black crappie has been recorded here. The provincial campground offers electrical sites, showers and a beach, suiting family trips.

lakes.name: Burge Lake
lakes.description: Burge Lake is a small drive-to lake about 10 km north of Lynn Lake, with a provincial park campground on its west shore. An Islands.com feature on the park notes that walleye and northern pike are plentiful in the lake. The park hosts an annual catch-and-release northern pike derby on Canada Day.

towns.name: Lynn Lake
towns.description: Lynn Lake is a small former mining town in northwestern Manitoba. It serves as a float-plane base for remote fly-in lodges and has basic groceries, fuel, and lodging for anglers.

lakes.name: Burntwood Lake
lakes.description: Burntwood Lake is a large northern lake fished through Burntwood Lake Lodge, a fly-in operation out of Winnipeg. The fishery centers on walleye and northern pike, with outcamp options on more remote water. The Manitoba Anglers' Guide lists lake-specific walleye and pike limits for the lake.

lakes.name: Caddy Lake
lakes.description: Caddy Lake sits on the Whiteshell River near the Ontario border and is famous for the rock tunnels under the rail lines that connect it to South Cross and North Cross lakes - paddling through them is a classic Whiteshell outing. The lake covers about 300 hectares with a maximum depth of 5.7 metres, and fishing yields master angler catches of walleye, northern pike, smallmouth bass, black crappie, rock bass and yellow perch. The province runs a seasonal campground on the west shore, and Green Bay Resort sits on the east shore.

lakes.name: Carroll Lake
lakes.description: Carroll Lake straddles the Manitoba-Ontario border (mostly in Ontario's Woodland Caribou Provincial Park, with Manitoba bays in Atikaki), stretching 20 km long on the Gammon River system. Wallace Lake Lodge flies anglers in for walleye, northern pike and perch in true backcountry solitude. MidWest Outdoors TV has filmed walleye episodes on the Manitoba side.

lakes.name: Childs Lake
lakes.description: The largest waterbody in Duck Mountain Provincial Park and its most developed fishing hub, with two boat launches, a filleting station, campground, yurts, and a lodge. It is one of the few lakes in the Ducks with a lake trout fishery, and anglers hit it hard in early spring and late fall for lakers. Walleye and pike fill the rest of the season, and burbot bite through the ice. Local cottagers are the best source of day-to-day intel.

lakes.name: Cormorant Lake
lakes.description: Cormorant Lake lies along Highway 10 between The Pas and Flin Flon. A Discover The Pas ice-fishing feature lists Nootin Resort on the lake, with northern pike, walleye, whitefish, and lake trout as the most common fish. It is a convenient drive-to northern fishery.

towns.name: Cormorant
towns.description: Cormorant is a small northern community along Highway 10 between The Pas and Flin Flon. Anglers reach Cormorant Lake through local resorts offering cabins and boat access.

lakes.name: Cranberry Lakes
lakes.description: The Cranberry Lakes are a chain of lakes near Cranberry Portage on the Grass River system. A Hunt Fish Manitoba blog describes walleye, pike, and lake trout as abundant throughout the chain, calling First Cranberry a walleye factory and Second Cranberry a laker lake. Viking Lodge on First Cranberry Lake offers cabins and guided fishing.

towns.name: Cranberry Portage
towns.description: Cranberry Portage is a small northern community at the junction of Highways 6 and 10. It is home to lodges on the Cranberry Lakes chain and a staging point for Grass River fishing trips.

lakes.description: A semi-remote Porcupine Forest lake popular with north-mountain anglers as an alternative to North Steeprock. It has an undeveloped launch and dock, and its abundant underwater structure makes a fish finder a big advantage for finding walleye and whitefish. Reached along the National Mills logging road, usually by 4x4 in summer.

towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle before the Porcupine Forest.

lakes.name: Deloraine Reservoir
lakes.description: A small reservoir east of Deloraine in Manitoba's far southwest, this water is known for outsized smallmouth bass, with 21-inch fish caught through both open water and ice. Unlike typical shield bass lakes, its smallies relate to shoreline vegetation and rip rap. Walleye are also present from provincial stocking, making it a legitimate two-species stop.

lakes.name: East Blue Lake
lakes.description: One of Manitoba's clearest and deepest park lakes, East Blue sits at the heart of Duck Mountain Provincial Park and draws anglers year-round. The spring-fed water is so clear the bottom stays visible 9-12 m down, and the deep basin holds lake trout while stocked rainbows and splake cruise shallower water. Gang trolling the deeps and bottom-bouncing for walleye are the proven tactics here. The Blue Lakes campground and resort offer full amenities right on the shore.

lakes.name: East Goose Lake
lakes.description: One of Roblin's signature 'Parkland Paradise' fisheries: a small, aerated, electric-motor-only lake with trophy trout, including the famous Markosky-strain rainbows. Rainbow and brown trout share the water with stocked walleye and perch. It has an undeveloped launch, angling docks, modern washrooms, and great access right off Hwy 83. Trout limit is one.

lakes.name: East Shoal Lake
lakes.description: East Shoal Lake is the easternmost of the three Shoal Lakes, a group of prairie lakes set between Lake Manitoba and Lake Winnipeg about an hour northwest of Winnipeg. It is relatively shallow and celebrated for yellow perch ice fishing, with northern pike as the secondary target. Higher water levels in recent years have boosted perch and pike numbers and reduced winterkill.

towns.name: Teulon
towns.description: Teulon is an Interlake town about 45 kilometres north of Winnipeg on Highway 7, with restaurants, services and a golf course. It is the main service centre for Norris Lake and the Shoal Lakes.

lakes.description: Edmund Lake is a small northern lake fished as an outpost of Elk Island Lodge on Gods Lake. Tripadvisor angler reviews confirm northern pike, lake trout, and walleye in the lake. It is a fly-in outpost destination for guests chasing multiple trophy species.

lakes.name: Elgin Reservoir
lakes.description: A stocked trout reservoir southwest of Brandon, Elgin Reservoir appears in the province's official stocked trout waters list. Angler reports show brown trout and tiger trout as the catches. It is a small, accessible stillwater trout option for Westman anglers who want trout without driving to the mountains or the Whiteshell.

A Master Angler sauger ranked number one for the lake shows it holds more than just walleye. This is backcountry water - bring everything you need.

lakes.name: Fishing Lake
lakes.description: A backcountry Porcupine Forest lake known for trophy walleye and northern pike over tons of underwater structure. Despite the long haul-trail access, the lake itself is family-friendly with great shoreline access and quality angling. Launch areas are restricted to small watercraft. Most commonly reached by snowmobile in winter; the summer trail is long and rough.

towns.name: Swan River
towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle before the Porcupine Forest.

lakes.name: Gass Lake
lakes.description: A Porcupine Hills brook trout water west of North Steeprock Lake, listed as a stocked trout water in the Angler's Guide. The province has stocked brook trout fingerlings here. It is remote forest country, so pair it with a North Steeprock trip for a full day.

towns.name: Swan River
towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle before the Porcupine Forest.

lakes.name: Glad Lake
lakes.description: A deep, clear lake near the Wellman campground that holds one of Manitoba's rare arctic char fisheries. Char were re-introduced in 2017 and an ongoing pike-transfer program helps protect them, alongside lake trout and pike. Trophy trout have been taken here over the years. Special regulations apply: all arctic char must be released. The Wellman Lake campground amenities are minutes away.

towns.name: Swan River
towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle before the park.

lakes.name: Goudney Reservoir
lakes.description: A small reservoir west of Pilot Mound on PR 253, Goudney Reservoir is a stocked walleye water covered by the province's southwestern walleye regulations. It is a low-key prairie reservoir for anglers working the smaller waters of the Pembina Valley. Expect modest walleye with little fishing pressure.

towns.name: Pilot Mound
towns.description: Small Pembina Valley town with basic services, fuel and groceries for anglers heading to Goudney Reservoir.

lakes.name: Grayling Lake
lakes.description: A Riding Mountain National Park lake listed by Parks Canada among its road-accessible northern pike waters. Like the park's other backcountry lakes, expect non-motorized access rules and a required national park fishing licence. It is one of the seed lakes worth checking if you are exploring the park beyond Clear Lake and Lake Audy.

towns.name: Wasagaming
towns.description: Riding Mountain National Park's townsite on Clear Lake, with shops, restaurants, boat services, and Parks Canada offices.

towns.name: Onanole
towns.description: Town at the park's east gate with motels, restaurants, and tackle.

lakes.name: Gull Lake
lakes.description: A multi-trout lake in the Childs Lake area of the Ducks, offering splake, rainbows, and brookies to fly and spin anglers alike. Perch numbers have been climbing, so expect bonus catches. An undeveloped launch, dock, filleting station, and day-use area make it an easy day trip. Big rainbows to 30 inches have come out of here.

towns.name: Swan River
towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle before the park.

towns.name: Grandview
towns.description: Town in the valley south of Duck Mountain Provincial Park, handy for anglers accessing the park's campgrounds.

lakes.name: Gull Lake
lakes.description: Gull Lake is a small, clear lake near Beaconia on the east shore of Lake Winnipeg's south basin, ringed by cottages. Anglers fish it for northern pike and small perch, and regulations require all pike over 60 cm to be released. Its calm, shallow water also makes it popular for kayaking and swimming.

towns.name: Beaconia
towns.description: Beaconia is a small community on the east shore of Lake Winnipeg's south basin, minutes from Gull Lake. It has a general store and seasonal cottaging services.
towns.distance: on Lake Winnipeg, near the lake

lakes.name: Happy Lake
lakes.description: Happy Lake is the third lake in the Quesnel chain inside Nopiming Provincial Park, sharing the system's trophy walleye, smallmouth bass, northern pike, perch and whitefish. The three-lake chain is drive-to accessible yet fishes like a northern fly-in lake. Q Lake Lodge at Caribou Landing is the only lodge on the chain.

towns.name: Manigotagan
towns.description: Small community at the mouth of the Manigotagan River on Lake Winnipeg's east shore; the river canoe route connects Caribou Landing to town.
towns.distance: downstream of the Quesnel chain on the Manigotagan River

lakes.name: Hunt Lake
lakes.description: Hunt Lake near West Hawk Lake is one of the Whiteshell's most reliable stocked trout fisheries, regularly stocked since the 1950s with brook trout the mainstay in recent decades plus periodic adult brook and brown trout for trophy potential. The 2024 provincial assessment describes a small lake (0.18 sq km, 13.1 m max depth) with a public dock and boat launch for electric or self-propelled craft. Special trout rules apply, including a limit of one and artificial lures and flies only. The lake is also the trailhead for the popular Hunt Lake hiking trail.

towns.name: West Hawk Lake
towns.description: Townsite in Whiteshell Provincial Park near the Ontario border; the closest community to the Caddy and Cross lake chain and the Hunt Lake trailhead.

regulations.special: No possession limit or size restriction for largemouth bass. Stocked trout water.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Jessica Lake
lakes.description: One of the Whiteshell's premier walleye lakes, Jessica Lake has received hundreds of thousands of stocked walleye fry nearly every year since 2010, and the province's 2022 fisheries assessment found walleye, smallmouth bass, black crappie, northern pike and yellow perch in its survey nets. The lake is also noted as an important traditional fishing area for Manitoba First Nations. Like most eastern Manitoba waters, it falls under the Area A rule that all walleye over 45 cm must be released.

towns.name: Rennie
towns.description: Small community in Whiteshell Provincial Park; the Whiteshell Natural History Museum operates nearby and the Alfred Hole Goose Sanctuary sits just east on Highway 44.

towns.name: Falcon Lake
towns.description: Townsite in Whiteshell Provincial Park on the Trans-Canada Highway, home to the Hotel at Falcon Lake and the closest full services for anglers fishing the park's eastern lakes.
towns.distance: townsite on the Trans-Canada in the Whiteshell

lakes.name: Kenton Reservoir
lakes.description: A small reservoir just south of the community of Kenton, stocked with walleye fry and covered by southwestern Manitoba walleye rules. It is a simple local water rather than a destination, useful for a quick evening trip. Small boat or shore fishing is the practical approach.

towns.name: Kenton
towns.description: Small community in western Manitoba; the reservoir sits just south of town.

lakes.name: Killarney Lake
lakes.description: A small, shallow lake right on the edge of the town of Killarney, Killarney Lake is an easy-access family fishery. Provincial depth charts list northern pike, walleye, black bullhead, yellow perch, white sucker and even largemouth bass as common species. It is stocked with walleye fry and fishes well for pike and panfish close to town amenities.

towns.name: Killarney
towns.description: Full-service southwestern Manitoba town with restaurants, groceries, fuel and lodging; the lake sits on its southwest side.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Southern Division limits apply.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Kiskittogisu Lake
lakes.description: Kiskittogisu Lake is a long, narrow lake on the west channel of the Nelson River, west of Playgreen Lake and southeast of Kiskitto Lake. Like Playgreen, it carries a fall commercial quota for walleye, sauger and lake whitefish fished by Norway House fishers. It is remote water reached by boat from Norway House or via Whiskey Jack Landing, with very little recreational angling pressure.

towns.name: Norway House
towns.description: Norway House is a Cree community on the Nelson River between Lake Winnipeg and Playgreen Lake, home to the Norway House Cree Nation. Its fishermen's co-op manages the commercial fishery on Playgreen and Kiskittogisu lakes, and the community's launches are the main boat access for anglers heading onto those waters.
towns.distance: east of the lake, on the Nelson River

lakes.name: Knee Lake
lakes.description: Knee Lake sits in the northern wilds about a 90-minute flight north of Winnipeg. North Star Resort is based on the lake, advertising trophy northern pike, walleye, and brook trout. It is a classic multi-species fly-in destination with very light fishing pressure.

lakes.name: Lake Audy
lakes.description: A well-known Riding Mountain National Park lake with a boat launch for motorized boats, listed by Parks Canada for northern pike fishing. Trout anglers also prize it for trophy rainbow trout in the deeper water near drop-offs and rocky areas. A national park fishing licence is required, and it is one of the park's easiest lakes to fish from a motorboat.

towns.name: Wasagaming
towns.description: Riding Mountain National Park's townsite on Clear Lake, with shops, restaurants, boat services, and Parks Canada offices.

towns.name: Onanole

lakes.name: Lake Irwin
lakes.description: A small lake just southeast of Neepawa, Lake Irwin is a stocked pike-and-perch water the province has supplemented with adult northern pike and perch. It is a simple, close-to-town option for a quick outing rather than a destination fishery. Expect modest-sized pike and perch with easy access from Neepawa.

towns.name: Neepawa
towns.description: Town northwest of Winnipeg with full services, restaurants and lodging; Lake Irwin is minutes away.

lakes.name: Lake Katherine
lakes.description: A Riding Mountain National Park lake listed by Parks Canada for road-accessible northern pike fishing, with non-motorized boats only. A national park fishing licence is required. Note this is the national park's Lake Katherine, not to be confused with the smaller Duck Mountain lake of the same name.

towns.name: Wasagaming
towns.description: Riding Mountain National Park's townsite on Clear Lake, with shops, restaurants, boat services, and Parks Canada offices.

lakes.name: Lake Metigoshe
lakes.description: A clear, spring-fed lake straddling the Canada-US border in the Turtle Mountains, Lake Metigoshe offers walleye, northern pike and perch in a scenic wooded setting. The Manitoba portion is quieter than the developed North Dakota side, with a public beach and the year-round Turtle Mountain Resort on the Canadian shore. It is a good multi-species lake for families who want fishing plus swimming and trails.

towns.name: Boissevain
towns.description: Gateway town to the Turtle Mountains with groceries, fuel and an outdoor shop; the nearest Manitoba service centre for the lake.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Southern Division limits apply.

lakes.name: Lake Minnewasta
lakes.description: A reservoir on Morden's west side and the centrepiece of the Lake Minnewasta Recreation Area, this lake offers walleye under a special size rule plus a notable black crappie population. It pairs fishing with a sandy beach, campground, and trail system, making it a strong family day-trip lake. Recent angler reports show steady crappie action.

towns.name: Morden
towns.description: Pembina Valley city with full services, restaurants and lodging; home to the Canadian Fossil Discovery Centre and the lake's recreation area.

lakes.name: Lake St. Andrews
lakes.description: Lake St. Andrews is a small, shallow lake just two kilometres from Lake St. George in the north Interlake. It is fished for northern pike and smallmouth bass, with bass under protective provincial limits. A tiny two-hectare provincial park on its west shore provides day-use access and a boat launch.

towns.name: Dallas
towns.description: Dallas is a small north-Interlake community about 33 kilometres south of Lake St. George. Its general store is where campers and anglers stock up on supplies before heading to the lake.

lakes.name: Lake St. George
lakes.description: Lake St. George is a north-Interlake drive-to lake about 176 kilometres north of Winnipeg, well known for walleye, northern pike and perch fishing. A provincial park campground with 28 basic sites plus a boat launch and dock sits on its shore, making it one of the most accessible walleye lakes in the northern Interlake. Special regulations protect larger fish: all walleye over 45 cm must be released.

lakes.name: Lake Wahtopanah
lakes.description: Also known as the Rivers Reservoir, Lake Wahtopanah is a reservoir on the Little Saskatchewan River just east of Rivers. Provincial surveys list walleye, northern pike, rock bass and perch as the common species, and index netting found walleye the dominant catch. It has produced Master Angler walleye and pike, hosts an annual summer fishing derby, and offers boat launches plus camping at Rivers Provincial Park.

towns.name: Rivers
towns.description: Town immediately west of the lake with the provincial park campground, boat launches, groceries and fuel.

towns.name: Brandon
towns.description: Manitoba's second-largest city with full services and tackle shops; the regional base for Wahtopanah anglers.

lakes.name: Laurie Lake
lakes.description: A bigger, deeper Duck Mountain stillwater famous for massive brown trout that can push 30 inches. The ultra-clear water demands a stealthy approach, but the browns, rainbows, and stocked walleye reward the effort. It is listed as a stocked trout water with a boat launch off PR 367. Guide outfitters run stillwater fly trips here regularly.

towns.name: Swan River
towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle before the park.

regulations.special: Stocked trout water (Duck Mountain); all trout smaller than 35 cm must be released.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Little Duck Lake
lakes.description: Little Duck Lake is a remote northern lake fished by The Lodge at Little Duck. The lodge's fishing page lists northern pike, lake trout, and arctic grayling as target species. It shares the pristine far-north character of nearby Nejanilini Lake.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Northeast Division limits apply.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Little Limestone Lake
lakes.description: Little Limestone Lake is the world's largest marl lake, famous for water that shifts from crystal clear to brilliant turquoise as calcite precipitates in warm weather. Beneath the Caribbean looks is a genuine fishery for walleye, northern pike, perch and lake whitefish, with very little angling pressure thanks to its remote setting off Highway 6. The whole lake sits in a backcountry provincial park, so visits take planning and permission from the Mosakahiken Cree Nation.

towns.name: Grand Rapids
towns.description: Grand Rapids is a northern Manitoba town at the mouth of the Saskatchewan River on Lake Winnipeg's north basin, built around the Grand Rapids Generating Station. It is the last full-service stop for fuel, groceries and lodging for anglers heading to Playgreen Lake and the lakes beyond.
towns.distance: south of the lake, on Hwy 6

lakes.name: Lyons Lake
lakes.description: Lyons Lake sits right off the Trans-Canada Highway near the Ontario border and is a go-to roadside rainbow trout spot, well stocked with rainbows in the 8-15 inch range plus big brood-stock brown trout from the hatchery. The government's depth map lists rainbow and brown trout as the common species and shows a maximum depth of 20.5 metres in just 0.23 square kilometres. Yellow perch, tiger trout and black bullheads also show up in angler catches.

towns.name: West Hawk Lake
towns.description: Townsite in Whiteshell Provincial Park near the Ontario border; the closest community to the Caddy and Cross lake chain and the Hunt Lake trailhead.

regulations.special: Stocked trout water (general stocked trout rules apply).
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Manigotagan Lake
lakes.description: Manigotagan Lake is the middle lake of the Quesnel chain, fished from Q Lake Lodge at Caribou Landing with the same trophy walleye, smallmouth bass, northern pike, perch and whitefish as Quesnel. The chain's three connected lakes give anglers a different lake to explore each day. Private island campsites are available on Manigotagan as well.

towns.name: Manigotagan
towns.description: Small community at the mouth of the Manigotagan River on Lake Winnipeg's east shore; the river canoe route connects Caribou Landing to town.
towns.distance: downstream of the Quesnel chain on the Manigotagan River

lakes.name: Mantagao Lake
lakes.description: Mantagao Lake is a north-Interlake lake set between Lake Manitoba and Lake Winnipeg, fished mainly by local anglers. Catch reports point to northern pike as the main target, with rock bass also present. It is a quiet, low-pressure alternative to the busier Shoal Lakes to the south.

towns.name: Hodgson
towns.description: Hodgson is a community in Manitoba's north Interlake on Highway 6. It serves as a gateway to the Lake St. George and Mantagao Lake area.

towns.name: Ashern
towns.description: Ashern is a north-Interlake town on Highway 6 with fuel, groceries, lodging and dining. It is a staging point for North Shoal Lake and Mantagao Lake.

lakes.name: Marge Lake
lakes.description: A Swan Valley-area walleye lake that the province and Swan Valley Sport Fishing have monitored for walleye recruitment in multiple years. It carries special regulations: walleye limit is 2 and all walleye shorter than 35 cm must be released. A quieter option for anglers exploring the Duck Mountain region's walleye waters.

towns.name: Swan River
towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle in the area.

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Mary Jane Reservoir
lakes.description: A small reservoir west of Manitou on the edge of the Pembina Valley, Mary Jane Reservoir is one of the few southern Manitoba waters managed specifically for black crappie, with a dedicated limit of four. Walleye are also present under the southwestern size rule. It is a niche panfish stop for anglers exploring the valley's smaller reservoirs.

towns.name: Manitou
towns.description: Small town with heritage sites and cafés; the reservoir is a short drive west.

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Max Lake
lakes.description: A Turtle Mountain lake at the south end of Highway 466, Max Lake is managed as a stocked walleye water with regular fry plants. It sits in the same forested Turtle Mountain country as the area's better-known bass and trout lakes. A quiet, small-boat lake best combined with a trip to nearby William or Bower lakes.

towns.name: Boissevain
towns.description: Gateway town to the Turtle Mountains with groceries, fuel and an outdoor shop; the service base for Max Lake.
towns.distance: nearest service town, south of the lake

lakes.name: McGavock Lake
lakes.description: McGavock Lake is part of the Laurie River system near Lynn Lake, fished by Laurie River Lodge. The lodge describes world-class northern pike, walleye, and lake trout across the system's connected lakes. Guests fly Winnipeg to Lynn Lake, then take a float plane to the lodge.

towns.name: Lynn Lake
towns.description: Lynn Lake is a small former mining town in northwestern Manitoba. It serves as a float-plane base for remote fly-in lodges and has basic groceries, fuel, and lodging for anglers.
towns.distance: float-plane base for Laurie River Lodge

lakes.name: Minnedosa Lake
lakes.description: A small reservoir on the Little Saskatchewan River at the town of Minnedosa, part of the same managed system as Lake Wahtopanah. Angler reports show northern pike, rock bass and walleye as the main catches, and the province stocks walleye fry here. Its special walleye regulation (all walleye over 45 cm released) reflects a quality-minded fishery close to town.

towns.name: Minnedosa
towns.description: Town on the Little Saskatchewan River with groceries, restaurants, fuel and lodging; the lake sits on its northeast side.

regulations.special: All walleye over 45 cm must be released (same rules as Wahtopanah Lake).
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Molson Lake
lakes.description: Molson Lake is a large northern lake fished through Molson Lake Lodge, listed in the Travel Manitoba and Hunt Fish Manitoba directories. The lodge targets northern pike, walleye, lake trout, and whitefish. Anglers fly in from Winnipeg to fish its productive waters.

towns.name: Norway House
towns.description: Norway House is a large Cree community at the north end of Lake Winnipeg. It provides fuel, groceries, and services for anglers heading to Molson Lake and other northern fisheries.

regulations.special: Stocked trout water (Porcupine Forest).
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Moon Lake
lakes.description: A road-accessible northern pike lake in Riding Mountain National Park, listed by Parks Canada among the park's pike fishing opportunities. Boats can be used but equipment must be carried in 300 m, and all personal watercraft are banned. A Manitoba national park fishing licence is required. Brown trout have also been reported here by trout anglers.

towns.name: Wasagaming
towns.description: Riding Mountain National Park's townsite on Clear Lake, with shops, restaurants, boat services, and Parks Canada offices.

towns.name: Onanole
towns.description: Town at the park's east gate with motels, restaurants, and tackle.

lakes.name: Moose Lake
lakes.description: Moose Lake near The Pas is a drive-to provincial park lake with a 59-site campground and boat launch. A Manitoba government fisheries assessment records northern pike, walleye, smallmouth bass, and yellow perch, with regular walleye stocking. The lake has produced Master Angler pike over 49 inches and walleye over 31 inches.

towns.name: The Pas
towns.description: The Pas is one of Manitoba's oldest communities, on the Saskatchewan River in the west-central north. It is a hub for drive-to northern fishing, with tackle shops, boat launches, guides, and highway access to nearby lakes.

lakes.name: Munroe Lake
lakes.description: Munroe Lake lies in the subarctic, roughly 1,000 km north of Winnipeg and 90 km south of the Nunavut border. Munroe Lake Lodge markets it as an untouched multi-species fishery for lake trout, northern pike, arctic grayling, and walleye. Hunt Fish Manitoba featured the lodge as a trophy destination with sight-fishing for giant pike.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general North Central Division limits apply.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Nejanilini Lake
lakes.description: Nejanilini Lake is a far-northern fly-in lake near the Nunavut border, fished by The Lodge at Little Duck. The lodge's fishing page lists northern pike, lake trout, and arctic grayling as target species. It is a pristine wilderness fishery with very light angling pressure.

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Neso Lake
lakes.description: Neso Lake is a northern lake off Highway 10 between The Pas and Flin Flon, fished through Neso Lake Lodge. The lodge advertises trophy northern pike and walleye as its headline species. It is a wilderness fishery with limited angling pressure.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Northwest Division limits apply.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Norris Lake
lakes.description: Norris Lake is a small, shallow Interlake lake between Teulon and Inwood that forms the headwaters of Netley Creek. Because the lake does not reliably hold fish through winter, the Teulon Fish and Game Association operates an aeration system to help populations survive. Anglers fish it for northern pike and yellow perch, and the provincial park campground on its northeast shore offers 15 basic sites.

towns.name: Teulon
towns.description: Teulon is an Interlake town about 45 kilometres north of Winnipeg on Highway 7, with restaurants, services and a golf course. It is the main service centre for Norris Lake and the Shoal Lakes.
towns.distance: 15 km east of the lake, via PR 17

towns.name: Inwood
towns.description: Inwood is a small Interlake community west of Teulon with a golf course. It sits close to Norris Lake Provincial Park and the Shoal Lakes.
towns.distance: adjacent; the park lies between Teulon and Inwood

lakes.name: North Cross Lake
lakes.description: North Cross Lake connects to South Cross Lake through a second rock tunnel under the CN line, making the Caddy-Cross chain a unique paddle-and-fish route. Angler reports list black crappie, northern pike and walleye. Like the rest of the Whiteshell, all walleye over 45 cm must be released.

towns.name: West Hawk Lake
towns.description: Townsite in Whiteshell Provincial Park near the Ontario border; the closest community to the Caddy and Cross lake chain and the Hunt Lake trailhead.

regulations.special: Nelson River from Whitemud Falls (Cross Lake outlet) to Kelsey Generating Station closed to lake sturgeon fishing May 1 to Jun 15.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: North Knife Lake
lakes.description: North Knife Lake is a remote fly-in trophy fishery in far northern Manitoba, reached by air from Winnipeg. Its cold, clear waters produce walleye, northern pike, lake trout, brook trout, arctic grayling, and whitefish. The lake is fished almost exclusively through North Knife Lake Lodge, which practices catch-and-release on trophy fish.

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: North Shoal Lake
lakes.description: North Shoal Lake is the northernmost of the Interlake's Shoal Lakes, sharing the group's famous yellow perch and northern pike fishing. Like West Shoal Lake, it has received stocked walleye. It is the least accessible of the three, fished mainly by boat in summer and by snowmobile in winter.

towns.name: Ashern
towns.description: Ashern is a north-Interlake town on Highway 6 with fuel, groceries, lodging and dining. It is a staging point for North Shoal Lake and Mantagao Lake.
towns.distance: south of the lake, on Hwy 6

lakes.name: North Steeprock Lake
lakes.description: Called Steeprock by locals, this big Porcupine Forest lake is a stunner with rocky shorelines and islands. Try the river portion for spring walleye, weedlines for summer pike, and steep contours for whitefish in early August. Two launches with docks, a filleting shack, and a basic campground serve anglers. Special regulations: walleye limit is 2 and all over 45 cm must be released. It can get rough on windy days.

towns.name: Swan River
towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle before the Porcupine Forest.

regulations.special: Walleye limit 2; all walleye over 45 cm must be released.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Nutimik Lake
lakes.description: Nutimik Lake on the Winnipeg River is one of the few Manitoba lakes where anglers can realistically target lake sturgeon - locals call them dinosaurs - alongside walleye, northern pike, smallmouth bass, perch and goldeye. Nutimik Lodge sits on the lake, and the provincial campground offers 98 sites near the Pine Point Rapids trail and Bannock Point petroforms. Remember sturgeon are catch-and-release.

towns.name: Rennie
towns.description: Small community in Whiteshell Provincial Park; the Whiteshell Natural History Museum operates nearby and the Alfred Hole Goose Sanctuary sits just east on Highway 44.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Southern Division limits apply.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Oak Lake
lakes.description: A classic prairie pothole lake west of Brandon, Oak Lake is one of southwestern Manitoba's most productive walleye fisheries. The province stocks around 800,000 walleye fry here each spring since natural reproduction is minimal, while northern pike and yellow perch reproduce on their own. It is famous for jumbo yellow perch alongside strong numbers of eater-sized walleye, and a full-service marina makes launching easy.

towns.name: Oak Lake
towns.description: Small community on the Trans-Canada Highway right by the lake, with fuel, a general store and the lake's marina.

towns.name: Brandon
towns.description: Manitoba's second-largest city with full services, tackle shops, restaurants and hotels; the standard base for Oak Lake trips.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Southern Division limits apply.

lakes.name: Obukowin Lake
lakes.description: Obukowin Lake is a Wallace Lake Lodge fly-in outpost lake, about a 35-minute flight from the Lac du Bonnet float base, with a two-bedroom housekeeping cabin on shore. The lodge describes incredible bottom structure holding large numbers of walleye, with northern pike in the weedy bays and channels among the islands. A nearby spring-fed lake with a cached boat is catch-and-release only.

towns.name: Lac du Bonnet
towns.description: Town on the Winnipeg River north of the Whiteshell; Manitoba Fisheries' eastern region office is based here.
towns.distance: floatplane base town for Wallace Lake Lodge outpost flights

towns.name: Bissett
towns.description: Small community in eastern Manitoba; Wallace Lake Lodge sits about 19 km east of town at the last drive-to entry into the Atikaki wilderness.

lodging.name: Wallace Lake Lodge & Outposts (Obukowin outpost cabin)

lakes.name: Patterson Lake
lakes.description: A FLIPPR stillwater trout factory on the south side of Riding Mountain, known worldwide for giant rainbows and browns. The aerated, electric-motor-only lake fishes best right after ice-out and again in late September and October, when all-day bites of trophy browns in the 20-25 inch range are not uncommon. Overnight camping is available on the lake.

towns.name: Oakburn
towns.description: Small community on Hwys 45/21 near Patterson and Tokaryk lakes in the Parkland.
towns.distance: 6.5 km north of the Hwy 45/21 junction at Oakburn

towns.name: Russell
towns.description: Town on the Yellowhead Hwy near Asessippi; the closest larger service town.

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Pelican Lake
lakes.size_text: 27.3 km² (2,734 ha); ~22 km long by 2.5 km wide
lakes.description: The largest navigable lake in southwestern Manitoba, Pelican Lake is a long, narrow prairie lake known first and foremost for walleye. The province stocks it heavily with walleye fry each year, and index netting shows walleye dominating the catch ahead of yellow perch and northern pike. It fishes well in both open water and winter, and the town of Ninette on the north shore hosts an annual walleye tournament.

towns.name: Ninette
towns.description: Small community on Pelican Lake's north shore and the lake's main service point, home to E & J Live Bait and several boat launches.

towns.name: Killarney
towns.description: Full-service town in southwestern Manitoba with groceries, fuel, restaurants and lodging, a short drive from Pelican Lake's east side.

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Perch Lake
lakes.description: A small Duck Mountain lake about 6.5 km north of East Blue Lake that has produced large brown trout up to 30 inches, plus smallmouth bass to 24 inches. Browns have been stocked here for years. Special regulations apply: all trout and bass must be released. Weighted nymphs and small leeches fished slow and deep are the fly-fishing ticket.

towns.name: Swan River
towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle before the park.

regulations.special: All trout must be released (Duck Mountain).
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Persse Lake
lakes.description: A 58-hectare stocked trout lake 37 km west-northwest of Roblin that has produced browns, rainbows, tigers, and stocked brookies. It is a listed stocked trout water with a trout limit of two and artificial lures/flies only. A solid Parkland stillwater option within easy reach of Roblin.

towns.name: Roblin
towns.description: Town at the junction of Hwys 5 and 83 near the Saskatchewan border, about 4 hours from Winnipeg; the hub for Parkland trout lakes and Lake of the Prairies access.

regulations.special: Trout limit 2; artificial lures/flies only.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Playgreen Lake
lakes.description: Playgreen Lake is a large, island-dotted widening of the Nelson River at the top of Lake Winnipeg, on the historic Norway House fur-trade corridor. It supports a commercial fishery run through the Norway House Fishermen's Co-op, with walleye, sauger and lake whitefish under quota. Anglers reach it by boat from Norway House or Grand Rapids and find classic shield-country structure with strong walleye and pike fishing.

towns.name: Norway House
towns.description: Norway House is a Cree community on the Nelson River between Lake Winnipeg and Playgreen Lake, home to the Norway House Cree Nation. Its fishermen's co-op manages the commercial fishery on Playgreen and Kiskittogisu lakes, and the community's launches are the main boat access for anglers heading onto those waters.
towns.distance: on the Nelson River between Lake Winnipeg and Playgreen Lake

towns.name: Grand Rapids
towns.description: Grand Rapids is a northern Manitoba town at the mouth of the Saskatchewan River on Lake Winnipeg's north basin, built around the Grand Rapids Generating Station. It is the last full-service stop for fuel, groceries and lodging for anglers heading to Playgreen Lake and the lakes beyond.
towns.distance: south of the lake, on the Saskatchewan River

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Quesnel Lake
lakes.description: Quesnel Lake anchors the Quesnel chain of lakes at the northern edge of Nopiming Provincial Park, served by the drive-to Q Lake Lodge at Caribou Landing. The lodge's waters hold trophy walleye, monster smallmouth bass, northern pike, perch and whitefish, and Hunt Fish Manitoba ranks the chain among Manitoba's best trophy fisheries for both walleye and smallmouth. Rental boats and private island campsites are available through the lodge.

towns.name: Manigotagan
towns.description: Small community at the mouth of the Manigotagan River on Lake Winnipeg's east shore; the river canoe route connects Caribou Landing to town.
towns.distance: downstream of the Quesnel chain on the Manigotagan River

lakes.name: Red Rock Lake
lakes.description: Red Rock Lake is a cottage lake of just over 500 acres along PR 307, about a dozen miles north of Rennie, with a Whiteshell River tributary flowing through it. Walleye have been stocked there for many years, joining northern pike, smallmouth bass, yellow perch, crappie and the occasional lake sturgeon. There are no park campgrounds - access is by car-top boat from Crown land - so it stays quieter than the busier Whiteshell lakes.

towns.name: Rennie
towns.description: Small community in Whiteshell Provincial Park; the Whiteshell Natural History Museum operates nearby and the Alfred Hole Goose Sanctuary sits just east on Highway 44.
towns.distance: lake lies about 12 miles north of town on PR 307

lakes.name: Reindeer Lake
lakes.description: Reindeer Lake straddles the Manitoba-Saskatchewan border and is one of the largest lakes in the region. Arctic Lodges operates on the lake, where anglers target northern pike, lake trout, walleye, and arctic grayling. Its vast, island-dotted waters are classic shield-country trophy habitat.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Northeast Division limits apply.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Rock Lake
lakes.description: A prairie lake in the Pembina Valley west of Pilot Mound, Rock Lake is a stocked walleye water that also holds northern pike and carp. Angler catch reports consistently show walleye and pike as the top species. It is a quieter alternative to the bigger name lakes nearby, with decent shore and small-boat access.

towns.name: Pilot Mound
towns.description: Small Pembina Valley town with basic services, fuel and groceries for anglers heading to Rock Lake and Goudney Reservoir.

regulations.special: Walleye limit 2; all walleye over 45 cm must be released.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Rocky Lake
lakes.description: Rocky Lake is a 26,000-acre drive-to lake about 30 minutes north of The Pas. The Travel Manitoba listing for Rocky Lake Cabins names northern pike, walleye, smallmouth bass, tullibee, whitefish, and perch in the lake. The resort offers cabins, camping, and boat and motor rentals, with nearby Clearwater Lake for lake trout.

towns.name: The Pas
towns.description: The Pas is one of Manitoba's oldest communities, on the Saskatchewan River in the west-central north. It is a hub for drive-to northern fishing, with tackle shops, boat launches, guides, and highway access to nearby lakes.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Northwest Division limits apply.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Rossman Lake
lakes.description: A small lake north of Rossburn on PR 577, Rossman Lake is a stocked walleye water under the southwestern walleye regulations. It is a quiet prairie lake for local anglers rather than a destination fishery. Fish it as part of a swing through the smaller walleye waters west of Riding Mountain.

towns.name: Rossburn
towns.description: Parkland town with basic services, groceries and fuel; Rossman Lake is minutes north.

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Sandy Lake
lakes.description: A stocked walleye lake near the town of Sandy Lake on the edge of Riding Mountain country. Angler reports show consistent catches of both walleye and northern pike, and the province's stocked-walleye assessments include it. The town of Sandy Lake offers basic services and puts you close to the national park and Vermilion Reservoir.

towns.name: Sandy Lake
towns.description: Town on the edge of Riding Mountain country with basic services for anglers.
towns.distance: at the town of Sandy Lake

towns.name: Dauphin
towns.description: City on Hwys 5/10 west of Riding Mountain with full services and tackle shops.

lakes.name: Sasa-Ginni-Gak Lake
lakes.description: Sasa-Ginni-Gak Lake lies in Atikaki Provincial Park in eastern Manitoba, reached only by air. Road Trip Manitoba's fishing guide lists walleye, northern pike, and lake trout for the lake. It is a remote wilderness fishery with virtually no angling pressure.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Northeast Division limits apply.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Sasaginnigak Lake
lakes.description: Sasaginnigak Lake in Atikaki Provincial Park is a big, diverse walleye lake where lodge guests report 24-29 inch walleye in quantity and 44-inch northern pike. Angler reports also list yellow perch. Sasa-ginni-gak Lodge and Outcamps operates cabins with boats, motors and fish finders on the lake.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Southern Division limits apply.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Shoal Lake
lakes.description: A 9-km-long Parkland lake with a stocked walleye and pike fishery, popular for boating and fishing. The community of Shoal Lake sits at the lake's north side, in the Rural Municipality of Yellowhead. It is an easy-access walleye option in western Manitoba's farm country, not far from Patterson and Tokaryk lakes.

towns.name: Shoal Lake
towns.description: Community on the lake's north side in the RM of Yellowhead with basic services.

towns.name: Russell
towns.description: Town on the Yellowhead Hwy; the closest larger service town.

lakes.name: Shoal Lakes (East & West)
lakes.description: The Interlake's Shoal Lakes (East, West and North) are among Manitoba's most famous jumbo-perch destinations, with winter perch over 15 inches drawing anglers from across the province. Northern pike are abundant and the lakes have been stocked with walleye as a bonus species. They are shallow prairie lakes with limited access, so a small boat is recommended in summer and the ice season is prime time.

towns.name: St. Laurent
towns.description: Interlake community on Lake Manitoba's east shore with lodging and services; the convenient base for West Shoal Lake trips.

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Shoe Lake
lakes.description: Shoe Lake is Nopiming's smallmouth bass numbers lake - anglers report catching smallies all day long, mostly 12-15 inches with a 19-inch fish a realistic bonus. Walleye are present but scarce these days, and the drive in is rough. Backcountry campsites and nearby Nopiming Lodge cabins serve visiting anglers.

towns.name: Bissett
towns.description: Small community in eastern Manitoba; Wallace Lake Lodge sits about 19 km east of town at the last drive-to entry into the Atikaki wilderness.

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Siderock Lake
lakes.description: Siderock Lake is fished through Wallace Lake Lodge, which lists walleye and northern pike as abundant in its waters and offers Siderock access from the main lodge. The province's angling guide has carried a Siderock-specific walleye limit, marking it as a managed walleye water. Expect a quiet, drive-to-plus-boat-in experience.

towns.name: Bissett
towns.description: Small community in eastern Manitoba; Wallace Lake Lodge sits about 19 km east of town at the last drive-to entry into the Atikaki wilderness.

lakes.name: Simonhouse Lake
lakes.description: Simonhouse Lake sits on the Grass River between the Cranberry lakes and Lake Athapapuskow. A Hunt Fish Manitoba feature highlights the Simonhouse Narrows for big numbers of walleye. It pairs well with a Cranberry Lakes trip for anglers chasing numbers.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Northwest Division limits apply.
regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Singush Lake
lakes.description: Singush is a shallower, walleye-stocked lake on the park's southeast side with a solid smallmouth bass population as well. The province has poured millions of walleye fry into it over the years, and the provincial bathymetric map lists walleye, pike, smallmouth, and perch. An established launch, filleting shack, and basic campground serve anglers, and the lake is quieter than Wellman or Childs.

towns.name: Swan River
towns.description: The Swan Valley's main service town on Hwy 10; the last full stop for groceries, fuel, and tackle before the park.

towns.name: Grandview
towns.description: Town in the valley south of Duck Mountain Provincial Park; turn west onto PR 367 just north of Garland to reach the lake.

lakes.name: Sipiwesk Lake
lakes.description: Sipiwesk Lake is a broad expansion of the upper Nelson River, flooded in 1961 by the Kelsey Generating Station. Experimental gillnet surveys have documented a rich fish community including walleye, northern pike, sauger, lake whitefish, perch, mooneyes and goldeye, and the area is recognized lake sturgeon habitat. It sits north of Cross Lake in remote, boat-access-only country.

towns.name: Cross Lake
towns.description: Cross Lake (Pimicikamak Cree Nation) is a community on the Nelson River south of Sipiwesk Lake. It is the nearest settlement for fuel and supplies, though Sipiwesk Lake itself is reached only by boat.
towns.distance: south of the lake, on the Nelson River

lakes.name: Snail Lake
lakes.description: A remote Porcupine Forest lake fished for arctic char, with fish that have made the Manitoba Master Angler record book. There is no summer land trail: reach it by canoe (a strenuous route, not for novices) or by snowmobile in winter, and launch areas are restricted to small watercraft. A true backcountry char trip for anglers willing to earn it.

lakes.name: South Cross Lake
lakes.description: South Cross Lake is reached from Caddy Lake by paddling through the historic CPR rail tunnel, a trip that draws sightseers as well as anglers. The government's 2022 assessment highlighted walleye, black crappie and yellow perch, with trophy-potential ratings for each. It shares the Area A rule requiring release of all walleye over 45 cm.

lakes.name: Southern Indian Lake
lakes.description: Southern Indian Lake is one of Manitoba's biggest northern lakes, known for walleye and northern pike action. The Opaskwayak Cree Nation tourism site highlights its world-class walleye and pike fishing plus trophy lake trout potential. Anglers typically access it through First Nations outfitters and remote camps.

lakes.name: Split Lake
lakes.description: Split Lake sits on the Nelson River in northeastern Manitoba. Fishbrain's lake profile lists walleye, northern pike, and sauger among its species. The Nelson River system's current and structure make it productive multi-species water.

lakes.name: Spray Lake
lakes.description: A small, crystal-clear Duck Mountain lake with walleye and pike that rewards sight-fishing in spring. The little red-and-white Five of Diamonds spoon is a local legend here. Walleye are periodically boosted with fry from the Beautiful Lake transfer program. It has a canoe/small-boat launch, angling dock, and hiking trail, and it is ideal for a quiet half-day trip.

lakes.name: St. Malo Lake
lakes.description: A stocked walleye lake beside the community of St. Malo in southeastern Manitoba, just east of PTH 59, provincially stocked with walleye fry. St. Malo Provincial Park on the lake offers campgrounds, new mini cabins and beaches with seasonal food service.

towns.name: St. Malo
towns.description: Franco-Manitoban community surrounding the provincial park, with the lake, campground and beach at its centre.

lakes.name: Star Lake
lakes.description: Star Lake is a smallmouth bass favourite in the Whiteshell - a Hunt Fish Manitoba day trip there produced endless medium-sized smallies plus a 23-inch walleye and a Master Angler black crappie in a single outing. The 2022 fisheries assessment found walleye, smallmouth bass, black crappie, northern pike, rock bass and yellow perch, with walleye fry stocked most years since 2011. The Nite Hawk Cafe sits just around the bend from the boat launch for a post-fishing meal.

lakes.name: Stephenfield Lake
lakes.description: A reservoir on the Boyne River inside Stephenfield Provincial Park, Stephenfield Lake is described by the province as a productive fishery with northern pike, perch and some walleye. It has a special walleye size rule (all walleye under 35 cm released). With a big family campground, sandy beach, boat launch and hiking trails, it is more of a camping-first lake where fishing is a strong bonus.

towns.name: Carman
towns.description: Pembina Valley town with full services, restaurants and golf courses; the main service centre for Stephenfield Provincial Park.

towns.name: Manitou
towns.description: Small town with heritage sites and cafés, closest community to the park's west side.

lakes.name: Stormon Lake
lakes.description: A small lake at the International Peace Gardens in Manitoba's extreme southwest corner, Stormon Lake has been stocked with adult northern pike. It is more of a curiosity stop for visitors to the Gardens than a serious fishery. Combine it with a trip to nearby Lake Metigoshe or the Turtle Mountains.

towns.name: Boissevain
towns.description: Gateway town to the Turtle Mountains and nearest Manitoba service centre for the Peace Gardens area.

lakes.name: Sturgeon Bay
lakes.description: Sturgeon Bay is a bay on the west shore of Lake Winnipeg's north basin near the mouth of the Dauphin River, in the Grand Rapids area. Walleye tagging studies have tracked fish moving through the bay, and anglers fish it from shore and boat for walleye and pike. Sturgeon Bay Provincial Park on Highway 8 offers a sandy beach, campground and boat launch.

towns.name: Grand Rapids
towns.description: Grand Rapids is a northern Manitoba town at the mouth of the Saskatchewan River on Lake Winnipeg's north basin, built around the Grand Rapids Generating Station. It is the last full-service stop for fuel, groceries and lodging for anglers heading to Playgreen Lake and the lakes beyond.

towns.name: Dauphin River
towns.description: Dauphin River First Nation is a small community at the mouth of the Dauphin River on Lake Winnipeg's north basin, about 3 kilometres from the lake. It sits beside the Sturgeon Bay fishery.
towns.distance: at the bay, on the Dauphin River

lakes.name: Swan Lake
lakes.description: A small lake in south-central Manitoba's Pembina Valley country, this Swan Lake (not the northern one) shows walleye and northern pike in angler catch reports. It is a low-pressure water without major development, suited to anglers exploring the smaller lakes of the region. Access is informal, so a small boat or shore setup is the practical approach.

regulations.source: 2026 Manitoba Anglers' Guide (gov.mb.ca/nrnd/fish-wildlife/pubs/fish_wildlife/fish/angling-guide.pdf), Waterbody Specific Regulations pp. 18-23

lakes.name: Tadoule Lake
lakes.description: Tadoule Lake is a vast, remote northern lake accessible only by air. Fishbrain's lake profile lists northern pike, walleye, and lake trout among its species. Its isolation and size make it a true wilderness trophy fishery.

regulations.note: No waterbody-specific rules listed — general Northeast Division limits apply.

lakes.name: Tokaryk Lake
lakes.description: A Parkland fly-fishing favourite that has earned a reputation as one of Canada's best stillwater trout fisheries, with brown trout and big rainbows. It sits 6.4 km north of Oakburn off PR 577, minutes from Patterson Lake. Perch and pike are also in the mix. Listed as a stocked trout water with a boat launch.

towns.name: Oakburn
towns.description: Small community on Hwys 45/21 near Patterson and Tokaryk lakes in the Parkland.

towns.name: Russell
towns.description: Town on the Yellowhead Hwy near Asessippi; Patterson Lake is about 60 km away.
